### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to enable tuning of Adaptive Parallel Encoding (APE) hyperparameters when no ground-truth labels are available for calibration. Paper [5] discusses estimating calibration error under label shift without labels, which aligns with the goal of label-free calibration. Paper [6] addresses hyperparameter tuning for pseudo-labeling in unsupervised domain adaptation, which also involves optimizing hyperparameters without labeled data. Both papers share the same problem-class level objective of label-free calibration or tuning.

### Mechanism
The contribution's mechanism minimizes KL divergence between sequential-teacher and parallel-encoded next-token distributions using model-internal distributional signals. Paper [3] proposes minimizing KL divergence under constraints for inference optimization, which is substantively equivalent to the KL minimization primitive. Paper [4] also minimizes KL divergence, specifically reverse KL, along diffusion trajectories, which involves a similar KL-based optimization approach. Paper [22] discusses inclusive KL minimization, which is another KL-based optimization paradigm. All three papers share the same underlying mechanism of KL divergence minimization.

### Evaluation
The contribution positions its method as a label-free proxy, with quantitative payoff reported in C2. Paper [5] evaluates calibration error without labels, which matches the label-free evaluation design. Paper [11] proposes a metric for unsupervised evaluation of domain adaptation models without target-domain labels, which also aligns with the label-free evaluation design. Both papers use the same evaluation design of validating methods without access to labeled data.

### Domain
The contribution operates in the domain of long-context LLM parallel context encoding. Papers [12] and [13] address parallel attention mechanisms for sequence-to-sequence learning and scene text recognition, which are substantively equivalent application areas involving parallel encoding in long-context settings. Both papers cover the same general domain.

Papers like [8] ("Label Shift Quantification with Robustness Guarantees via Distribution Feature Matching") and [4] ("Adaptive Symmetrization of the KL Divergence") use KL divergence for optimization and robustness analysis, but neither applies it to APE hyperparameter tuning or directly compares KL-based tuning to label-based tuning. No prior paper matches this mechanism.

### Evaluation
The evaluation design uses a downstream QA metric (F1 score) on LongBench 2WikiMultihopQA to validate the robustness of KL-tuned APE. Papers like [11] ("Automatic Prompt Engineering for Automatic Scoring") and [20] ("Submodular Evaluation Subset Selection in Automatic Prompt Optimization") use downstream task performance metrics to evaluate APE frameworks, which is substantively equivalent to the evaluation design here. The specific benchmark (LongBench 2WikiMultihopQA) is new, but the evaluation design (downstream task performance comparison) is covered.

### Domain
The domain is long-context multi-hop QA, specifically LongBench 2WikiMultihopQA. Papers like [13] ("Large language models encode clinical knowledge") and [11] ("Automatic Prompt Engineering for Automatic Scoring") address QA tasks, including multi-hop reasoning, though not specifically long-context QA or the LongBench dataset. However, the general application area of QA, including multi-hop reasoning, is covered.
